variants.name: Express view engine (EJS / Handlebars-compatible)
variants.implementation_notes: Server-side JavaScript keeps markup in files under views/ and renders it through an Express-compatible engine: app.set('view engine', 'ejs') then res.render('orders', model), with the engine's syntax for holes (<%= row.name %> in EJS, {{row.name}} in Handlebars/hbs) and includes or partials for chrome. EJS escapes with <%= and not with <%-; Handlebars escapes {{ }} by default and needs triple braces for raw HTML.
variants.idiom_name: Express res.render with an EJS/Handlebars view engine
pitfalls: EJS's <%- (and Handlebars' {{{ }}} ) opt out of escaping; one of them over user data is an XSS hole.
Express caches templates only when view caching is enabled (production), and Node caches required modules, so a fixed template can appear unfixed in development until restart.
Engines execute template code inside the server process: never render templates authored by end users.

variants.name: Backtick template literals with ${} holes (tagged for escaping)
variants.implementation_notes: The language itself supplies markup-with-holes: a backtick template literal keeps its indentation and interpolates with ${expression}, and a tagged template - a function that receives the literal's static parts and values separately - can implement escaping or HTML building. This is the zero-dependency realization for in-code fragments and small pages; move to an engine once templates are edited outside the code or need layouts, partials and loops.
variants.idiom_name: tagged template literal as an escaping html`` helper
pitfalls: An untagged literal escapes nothing: building a page from user-controlled values with plain ${} is an XSS hole, so interpolate through a tagged helper that escapes.
A tag function receives values as whole arguments, not element by element, so escaping per item (e.g. inside a mapped array) has to be done by the caller's helper.
Templates in code are not editable by markup authors and need a redeploy - the file-based motivation of the pattern is lost.
